extracted.intended_audience: potters, ceramic manufacturers, decorators, and informed readers interested in porcelain production
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance on the nature of porcelain, its defining materials (kaolin and feldspar), preparation and purification of raw materials, firing and glazing processes, and how composition choices affect workability, strength, and suitability for decoration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between porcelain, earthenware, and delf
rubrics_metrics.description: Porcelain is distinct from earthenware and delf: while earthenware is soft, opaque, and of impure colors, and delfs are earthenwares glazed with a leaden enamel rendered opaque by tin, hard porcelain is always white, perfectly clear, and is harder than steel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these visual and physical properties (whiteness, transparency/clearness, and high hardness) to identify true hard porcelain versus tender porcelain or other wares.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental constituent materials and their roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Hard porcelain is obtained from a white clay, kaolin, and is enameled with feldspar. Kaolin is a natural hydrated silicate of alumina that is absolutely refractory and opaque and constitutes the resistant part of porcelain; feldspars are silicates of alumina and potassa that are fusible at high temperature into a transparent glass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design formulations recognizing kaolin provides structure and resistance while feldspar melts to form the superficial glaze and increase clearness; successful porcelain relies on the complementary action of both.

rubrics_metrics.name: Firing process and chemical action
rubrics_metrics.description: If a mixture of kaolin and feldspar is covered with feldspar and heated at a very high temperature, the feldspar will melt and communicate to the opaque clay a greater clearness and a beautiful glaze; part of the action is chemical, producing a new crystalline silicate formed by combination of the substances present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control firing temperature and the presence of feldspar to achieve the desired clearness and glaze; recognize that both physical melting and chemical reactions (new silicate formation) determine final properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tender (soft) porcelain vs hard (kaolinic) porcelain
rubrics_metrics.description: Tender porcelain contains neither kaolin nor feldspar but is an artificial product (a kind of glass) made from sand, lime, potash, soda, and a small quantity of marine marl; it is baked without glazing and covered after baking with a glaze composed of silica, lead, potash, and soda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tender porcelain, though not true porcelain, has advantages for decoration (beauty, perfect glaze, facile fixing of colors) and thus is especially adapted to decorative work; choose tender vs hard porcelain according to artistic vs structural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purification and preparation of natural kaolin
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural kaolin contains impurities (sand, undecomposed feldspar, etc.) and must be purified: the mass is pounded and products separated by successive levigations with water; the extremely slow-settling clay is drawn off first and may be obtained almost pure, while other deposits are brayed in mills for pastes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ mechanical purification (pounding, levigation, settling, braying) to obtain kaolin grades appropriate for the intended paste; purity affects workability and final material properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust composition to intended use and properties
rubrics_metrics.description: The physical and chemical properties of porcelain vary infinitely according to the proportion of kaolin and feldspar and any added substances (lime, silicious sands, potsherds, etc.). Generally, porcelain is more solid as the proportion of clay increases and requires a higher baking temperature; increasing feldspar makes it more fusible, allows baking at lower temperature, and makes decoration easier, but reduces plasticity and ease of working.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the kaolin:feldspar ratio (and any additives) based on required resistance, firing schedule, and the kind of decoration anticipated; different factories and countries adopt compositions suited to specific functional and decorative aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of thorough mixing and mass stability
rubrics_metrics.description: The mixture of the materials should be perfect; when this is the case, the mass will keep for a long time and become (workable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure homogeneous mixing to improve storage stability and maintain consistent workability and firing behavior of the paste over time; imperfect mixing degrades performance.
